title.narrative: UNICEF - Education for green skills and climate action 2024-2027
UNICEF - Education for green skills and climate action 2024-2027

description.narrative:
Overall objective: Pre-schools, schools, science and public institutions empower children, adolescents and young people boys and girls - with green skills, enabling them to protect the environment and take climate action in their communities and beyond
1. Pre-school stakeholders countrywide with strengthened resources and skills, support young children, boys and girls, to acquire green skills and habits 2. The Experiential Learning Network with strengthened capacities expands the breadth and reach of its programmes to children and teachers with focus on rural and vulnerable communities 3. Vocational training stakeholders and public institutions provide improved teaching and practical instruction in science and green skills 4. Adolescents and young climate advocates, particularly girls, employ newly developed green skills to develop innovative climate action solutions in their communities

Overall result: Pre-schools, schools, science and public institutions empower children, adolescents and young people – boys and girls - with green skills, enabling them to protect the environment and take climate action in their communities and beyond
1. Pre-school stakeholders countrywide with strengthened resources and skills, support young children, boys and girls, to acquire green skills and habits
2. The Experiential Learning Network with strengthened capacities expands the breadth and reach of its programmes to children and teachers with focus on rural and vulnerable communities
3. Vocational training stakeholders and public institutions provide improved teaching and practical instruction in science and green skills
4. Adolescents and young climate advocates, particularly girls, employ newly developed green skills to develop innovative climate action solutions in their communities

Övergripande resultat: Förskolor, skolor, vetenskap och offentliga institutioner ger barn och ungdomar – pojkar och flickor – grön kompetens, vilket gör det möjligt för dem att skydda miljön och vidta klimatåtgärder i sina samhällen och utanför
1. Förskolans intressenter över hela landet med stärkta resurser och kompetens, stödjer små barn, pojkar och flickor att skaffa sig gröna färdigheter och vanor
2. Nätverket för erfarenhetsbaserat lärande med stärkt kapacitet utökar bredden och räckvidden för sina program till barn och lärare med fokus på landsbygden och utsatta samhällen
3. Yrkesutbildningsintressenter och offentliga institutioner tillhandahåller förbättrad undervisning och praktisk undervisning i naturvetenskap och gröna färdigheter
4. Ungdomar och unga klimatförespråkare, särskilt flickor, använder nyutvecklade gröna färdigheter för att utveckla innovativa klimatåtgärdslösningar i sina samhällen.

Key results:
- UNICEF has secured complementary funding from NELT, a private sector donor, pledging over 300,000 USD to support climate change education in the country. Through this partnership, UNICEF aims to enhance the competencies of vocational education and training students by organizing practical instruction (work-based learning) and summer practice (internships), with a specific focus on environment and climate change.
- 24 green vocational training curricula have been developed in 2025, with an additional 6 to be developed in 2026. To date, 1000 secondary school teachers have been trained to apply the new programmes, which are being rolled out to students across the country. Updated figures on student participation will be available in 2026.
- Over 20 primary school curricula from across disciplines now include content on environment and climate (up to 8th grade, 9th grade is still not covered). Updated figures on students learning under these new curricula will be available in 2026.
- 9 new elective subjects in primary school are specifically targeting environmental sustainability and climate change these are available in 5 languages of instruction. E.g. Environmental protection, Global warming and climate change, Energy and the environment, Living organisms and the environment.
- The Experiential Learning Network piloted within the previous phase has as of August 2025 been integrated into the bylaw that describes eligible institutions and sites for field trips and extracurricular activities. 6 new members (Biotechnology Laboratory, Ambicon air quality modeling lab, Seismological Observatory at Natural Sciences Faculty, CED Tearce, Artpoint Gumno, Polymath 13) have been added to the network, bringing the current number to 11 scientific institutions and civil society organizations. An additional 2 organizations (Educational Center Vevcani, operated by CSO Eko-svest and Science for children, operated by the Kantarot Foundation) are currently being considered for membership.
- The UPSHIFT youth innovation for climate programme, implemented on a project basis in the previous phase is now being institutionalized into the regular secondary school system. A formal curriculum is being prepared in collaboration with the Bureau for Development of Education.
Other results:
- UNICEF has integrated climate action, education and youth participation as key pillars of its new Country Programme Document. While not an outcome per se, this ensures that the project objectives are also UNICEF's own strategic priorities over the coming period.
- UNICEF has facilitated the integration of programme objectives and activities into the Annual Work Plans (2025) of the following Ministries: 1) Ministry of Education and Science (MoES) 2) Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning (MoEPP) 3) Ministry of Social Policy, Demographics and Youth (MSPDY)
- Project deliverables have been reflected in the annual activity plan of Bureau for Development of Education, including revision of Early Learning and Development curriculum, and integration of content from the GLOBE program implemented by the Ministry for Environment and Physical Planning
- In February 2025, the ELN organized a workshop focused on the practical application of the Guidelines for Adapting Experiential Learning Workshop Activities for Children with Disabilities and the adaptation of selected educational activities and experiments from the ELN program to better support students with disabilities.
- During the reporting period, 37 public institutions were selected to provide internship opportunities for students in the environment sector and related natural science disciplines such as biology, chemistry, geography. Through these opportunities for practical instruction, students will gain experience in a real workplace and develop green skills necessary for transitioning to a green economy. The students will be supported by 70 nominated mentors from the aforementioned institutions.
- In March 2025 UNICEF organized a meeting with the University of Shtip to explore possible partnerships with their newly established new maker space and accelerator programme. The University showed interest and resources to act as an UPSHIFT hub for the eastern part of the country and already signed MoUs with surrounding secondary schools.
- Over 230,000 people were reached with posts and messages on climate education and environmental health since October 2024, including posts on youthled climate calls to action as part of World Children's Day, information on the effects of air pollution on children and advice for parents, as well as the impact of air pollution on the most vulnerable families living with multiple deprivations.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
